arxiv-1404-2028.title: Large phase shift of (1+1)-dimensional nonlocal spatial solitons in lead glass
arxiv-1404-2028.creator: Qian Shou, Miao Wu, Qi Guo
arxiv-1404-2028.description: Abstract The large phase shift of strongly nonlocal spatial optical soliton(SNSOS) in the (1+1)-dimensional [(1+1)D] lead glass is investigated using the perturbation method. The fundamental soliton solution of the nonlocal nonlinear Schödinger equation(NNLSE) under the second approximation in strongly nonlocal case is obtained.

arxiv-2104-08930.title: Construction of higher-order metric fluctuation terms in spacetime symmetry-breaking effective field theory
arxiv-2104-08930.creator: Quentin G. Bailey
arxiv-2104-08930.description: Abstract We examine the basic conservation laws for diffeomorphism symmetry in the context of spontaneous diffeomorphism and local Lorentz-symmetry breaking. The conservation laws are used as constraints on a generic series of terms in an expansion around a flat background. We find all such terms for a two-tensor coupling to cubic order in the metric and tensor field fluctuations.

arxiv-2207-08181.title: Federated Continual Learning through distillation in pervasive computing
arxiv-2207-08181.creator: Anastasiia Usmanova, François Portet, Philippe Lalanda, German Vega
arxiv-2207-08181.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Anastasiia Usmanova, François Portet, Philippe Lalanda, German Vega. Federated Learning has been introduced as a new machine learning paradigm enhancing the use of local devices. At a server level, FL regularly aggregates models learned locally on distributed clients to obtain a more general model. Current solutions rely on the availability of large amounts of stored data at the client side in order to fine-tune the models sent by the server.

arxiv-2211-06551.title: Gaussian fluctuations of spatial averages of a system of stochastic heat equations Thanks: David Nualart was supported by the NSF grant DMS-2054735.
arxiv-2211-06551.creator: David Nualart, Bhargobjyoti Saikia
arxiv-2211-06551.description: Abstract . We consider a system of d d non-linear stochastic heat equations driven by an m m -dimensional space-time white noise on ℝ + × ℝ {\mathbb{R}}_{+}\times{\mathbb{R}} . In this paper we study the asymptotic behavior of spatial averages over large intervals [ − R , R ] [-R,R] .

arxiv-2404-00131.title: Give Text A Chance: Advocating for Equal Consideration for Language and Visualization
arxiv-2404-00131.creator: Chase Stokes, Marti A. Hearst
arxiv-2404-00131.description: Abstract Visualization research tends to de-emphasize consideration of the textual context in which its images are placed. We argue that visualization research should consider textual representations as a primary alternative to visual options when assessing designs, and when assessing designs, equal attention should be given to the construction of the language as to the visualizations.

arxiv-2407-16171.title: Learning Trimodal Relation for Audio-Visual Question Answering with Missing Modality
arxiv-2407-16171.creator: Kyu Ri Park, Hong Joo Lee, Jung Uk Kim
arxiv-2407-16171.description: Abstract Recent Audio-Visual Question Answering (AVQA) methods rely on complete visual and audio input to answer questions accurately. However, in real-world scenarios, issues such as device malfunctions and data transmission errors frequently result in missing audio or visual modality. In such cases, existing AVQA methods suffer significant performance degradation.

arxiv-2508-06770.title: Bounds on skew dimensions and characters of symmetric groups via thick hook decompositions
arxiv-2508-06770.creator: Lucas Teyssier
arxiv-2508-06770.description: Abstract We introduce a new decomposition of Young diagrams into thick hooks. These thick hook decompositions enable having a better control over hook products for excited diagrams in the Naruse hook length formula, which leads to improved bounds on the number of standard tableaux of skew shapes.

arxiv-2510-02607.title: Homotopy Languages
arxiv-2510-02607.creator: César Bardomiano Martínez, Simon Henry
arxiv-2510-02607.description: Abstract We attach to each weak model category ℳ \mathcal{M} a class of first order formulas about the fibrant objects of ℳ \mathcal{M} whose validity is invariant under homotopies and weak equivalences. This is a generalization of the classical Blanc-Freyd Language of categories—which involves formula avoiding equality on objects and which are invariant under isomorphism and equivalences of categories.

arxiv-2511-08958.title: Space-Efficient and Output-Sensitive Algorithms for the Longest Common Bitonic Subsequence
arxiv-2511-08958.creator: Md. Tanzeem Rahat, Md. Manzurul Hasan
arxiv-2511-08958.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Md. Tanzeem Rahat, Md. Manzurul Hasan. The longest common bitonic subsequence (LCBS) of two sequences A A and B B is the longest subsequence that increases to a single peak and then decreases while appearing, in order, in both inputs. Although LCBS naturally models “rise–fall” patterns in bioinformatics, finance and signal analysis, the only previously documented solution was the quadratic dynamic programme that needs Θ ⁡ ( n ​ m ) \Theta(nm) time and space.

arxiv-2512-20436.title: Dual-Encoder Transformer-Based Multimodal Learning for Ischemic Stroke Lesion Segmentation Using Diffusion MRI
arxiv-2512-20436.creator: Muhammad Usman 1 , Azka Rehman 2 , Muhammad Mutti Ur Rehman 3 , Abd Ur Rehman 4 , Muhammad Umar Farooq 5
arxiv-2512-20436.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Muhammad Usman 1 , Azka Rehman 2 , Muhammad Mutti Ur Rehman 3 , Abd Ur Rehman 4 , Muhammad Umar Farooq 5. Accurate segmentation of ischemic stroke lesions from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for timely clinical decision-making, treatment planning, and longitudinal outcome assessment. Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI) and Apparent Diffusion Coefficient (ADC) scans provide complementary information regarding acute and sub-acute ischemic changes; however, reliable automated delineation of infarct regions remains challenging due to variability in lesion size, shape, and location.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-goar.title: St. Goar (Catholic Encyclopedia article)
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-goar.creator: Léon Clugnet
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-st-goar.description: Article 'St. Goar' from the Catholic Encyclopedia (1913), the 15-volume English-language reference work published 1907-1914 by Robert Appleton Company.

pmc-10520361.title: Stacks of monogalactolipid bilayers can transform into a lattice of water channels
pmc-10520361.creator: Jakub Hryc, Michal Markiewicz, Marta Pasenkiewicz-Gierula
pmc-10520361.description: SummaryThe lipid matrix of thylakoid membranes is a lamellar bilayer, but under a certain condition it can convert locally into a nonlamellar structure. This is possible because one of the main membrane lipids, MGDG, promotes the formation of an inverse hexagonal phase.

pmc-10719341.title: Biophosphorescence in fluorescent millipedes (Diplopoda: Xystodesmidae) and its relationships with bioluminescence
pmc-10719341.creator: Vadim R Viviani
pmc-10719341.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Three types of luminescence have been reported in living organisms: bioluminescence (BL), ultraweak chemiluminescence and biofluorescence (FL). In millipedes, both BL and FL have been reported in Motyxia sequoiae and related Xystodesmidae species. Noteworthy, when walking at night with a UV lantern at the Biological Station of Highlands, I found three blue-fluorescent millipedes (Deltotaria brimleii, Deltotoria sp and Euryus orestes) that also displayed phosphorescence after turning off the UV source.

pmc-11314013.title: Chlorogenic Acid as a Promising Tool for Mitigating Chilling Injury: Cold Tolerance and the Ripening Effect on Tomato Fruit (Solanum lycopersicum L.)
pmc-11314013.creator: Mihaela Iasmina Madalina Ilea, Pedro Javier Zapata, Christian Fernández-Picazo, Huertas María Díaz-Mula, Salvador Castillo, Fabián Guillén, Enrico Doria
pmc-11314013.description: Tomato fruit (Solanum lycopersicum L.) has a very brief storability, displaying chilling injury (CI) when stored in cold conditions used to delay ripening. For this reason, in this study, different concentrations (10, 50, and 100 mg L−1) of chlorogenic acid (ChA) were assayed to evaluate its effectiveness in maintaining fruit quality traits and mitigating CI symptoms in tomatoes.

pmc-11399498.title: The role of facial distinctiveness in the prioritisation of targets in disjunctive dual-target face search
pmc-11399498.creator: Emma Smillie, Natalie Mestry, Dan Clark, Neil Harrison, Nick Donnelly
pmc-11399498.description: Two experiments explored the search for pairs of faces in a disjunctive dual-target face search (DDTFS) task for unfamiliar face targets. The distinctiveness of the target was manipulated such that both faces were typical or distinctive or contained one typical and one distinctive target. Targets were searched for in arrays of eight faces.

pmc-11462761.title: Ultra-processed foods intake in relation to metabolic health status, serum brain-derived neurotrophic factor and adropin levels in adults
pmc-11462761.creator: Donya Poursalehi, Shahnaz Amani Tirani, Farnaz Shahdadian, Zahra Hajhashemy, Parisa Rouhani, Parvane Saneei
pmc-11462761.description: BackgroundIn recent years, there has been a lot of discussion over the impact of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) intake on overall health of subjects. However, the association between UPFs intake and metabolic unhealthy (MU) status is still in a state of ambiguity.

pmc-11523101.title: Using artificial intelligence (AI) to assess the prevalence of false or misleading health-related claims
pmc-11523101.creator: Les Rose, Susan Bewley, Mandy Payne, David Colquhoun, Simon Perry
pmc-11523101.description: Complementary healthcare in the United Kingdom is subject to voluntary, publicly funded regulation. Many such practices include pseudoscience. There are concerns that regulated practitioners make misleading health claims. This study used an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to measure the prevalence of such claims.

pmc-11621403.title: Impact of electronic cigarette vaping on the cardiovascular function in young and old rats
pmc-11621403.creator: Wangde Dai, Jianru Shi, Juan Carreno, Michael T. Kleinman, David A. Herman, Rebecca J. Arechavala, Samantha Renusch, Irene Hasen, Amanda Ting, Robert A. Kloner
pmc-11621403.description: BackgroundWhile the acute exposure to electronic cigarette (E-cig) vapor has been associated with an increase in blood pressure, the chronic effect of E-cig vapor on blood pressure compared to standard cigarette smoke has not been extensively studied. We determined the effect of E-cig exposure on blood pressure and other measures of cardiac function in both young and old rats.

pmc-11859600.title: Childhood trauma as a predictor of social cognition disturbances across psychosis spectrum: Data from the PREGAP Study
pmc-11859600.creator: C. Aymerich, A. Catalan
pmc-11859600.description: IntroductionChildhood trauma is a severe form of stress that has been strongly related to both the appearance of a psychotic disorder and the existance of social cognition disturbances. We hereby hypothesize childhood trauma might be a transdiagnostic marker of social cognition disturbances across the psychosis spectrum, regardless of the main diagnosis.

pmc-12445062.title: Pseudopatella Identified in Bilateral Gonarthrosis: A Case Report of Preoperative Recognition and Surgical Considerations in Total Knee Arthroplasty
pmc-12445062.creator: Muhammed Yusuf Afacan, Mohammadreza Hajizadeh, Arın Celayir, Cumhur Deniz Davulcu, Nuri Aydin
pmc-12445062.description: Pseudopatella is a rare ossification within the quadriceps tendon, often associated with chronic mechanical stress or degenerative knee conditions, such as gonarthrosis. We report the case of a 59-year-old patient with bilateral gonarthrosis who underwent cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Intraoperatively, a pseudopatella was identified within the quadriceps tendon.

pmc-12811038.title: User Preferences for an Image-Assisted Dietary Recall: Qualitative Study Comparing 3 Dietary Assessment Methods
pmc-12811038.creator: Janelle D Healy, Christina M Pollard, Clare E Collins, Barbara A Mullan, Megan E Rollo, Satvinder S Dhaliwal, Richard Norman, Sharon I Kirkpatrick, Tracy A McCaffrey, Clare Whitton, Amira Hassan, Fengqing Zhu, Deborah A Kerr, Karthik Adapa, Laura A Bardon, Tom Baranowski, Annie W Lin
pmc-12811038.description: BackgroundTechnology-assisted 24-hour dietary recall (24HR) methods offer the potential for scalable population dietary assessment, but current challenges include balancing accuracy and cost against participant burden and acceptability of these methods. Qualitative methods present a novel approach to understanding potential barriers and enablers to the acceptability of 24HR methods, but remain relatively unexplored.

pmc-13266112.title: Synergistic Effects of SGLT2 Inhibitors and GLP-1R Agonists on Inflammation-Associated Oxidative Stress in Atrial Fibrillation
pmc-13266112.creator: Walaa Fakih, Ali Mroueh, Shinnosuke Kikuchi, Halim Marzak, Said Amissi, Dal-Seong Gong, Sophie Kerth, Michel Kindo, Arnaud Mommerot, Michael Paul Pieper, Patrick Ohlmann, Olivier Morel, Valérie Schini-Kerth, Laurence Jesel
pmc-13266112.description: Visual AbstractKey Words: atrial fibrosis, atrial remodeling, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor, inflammation, oxidative stress, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia. It is a major cause of stroke and is strongly associated with heart failure (HF), particularly HF with preserved ejection fraction.

pmc-13429821.title: Validation of Predictive Equations for Estimating Lean Soft Tissue and Fat-Free Mass in Class II–V Obesity: A Multicenter Observational Study with Implications for Bariatric Surgery Monitoring
pmc-13429821.creator: Alejandro Gómez-Bruton, Helder Fonseca, Susana Ara-Gimeno, Angel Matute-Llorente, Lucas Veras, Gabriel Lozano-Berges, Cláudia Mendes, Jorge Bravo, Manuel Carvalho, Pilar Irún, Ana Moradell, Maria Jose Palacios Fanlo, Marta Sánchez-Luengo, Gonzalo Hijos-Mallada, German Vicente-Rodríguez, Armando Raim
pmc-13429821.description: BackgroundPreoperative analysis of body composition is critical for anticipating metabolic changes and optimizing outcomes after bariatric surgery (BS). This study assessed agreement between dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived fat-free mass (FFM) and lean soft tissue (LST) and estimates from anthropometric equations in individuals with class-II obesity or greater.
